9. Push metadata filters into every channel (inverted-index clauses, filtered HNSW such as ACORN or vendor pre-filter, candidate filtering for late interaction), never post-filter the fused top-k; enforce tenant/ACL filters as mandatory server-side constraints that the planner cannot remove.

10. Query-side enhancements are pluggable 'query transforms' with a router: spelling/identifier normalization (always), acronym expansion from a company glossary (always, cheap), HyDE / Query2doc (gated by ambiguity or low first-stage score dispersion, cached), multi-query decomposition (delegated to the Task Decomposition model). Each transform records what it changed for provenance.

11. Corpus-size router: if the filtered collection is under ~200k tokens, bypass retrieval and hand the whole corpus to the generator with prompt caching (Anthropic); for mid-size, hybrid without reranker; for large, full cascade.

12. Observability: log per stage latency, candidate counts, score distributions, channel agreement (overlap of top-k between channels is a useful drift signal), fused vs reranked rank changes, filter selectivity, cache hit rates, and cost; sample queries with low reranker max score for human review and golden-set growth.

13. Evaluation is a first-class subsystem: BEIR-format datasets per collection (corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, qrels.tsv), nightly runs of nDCG@10/Recall@100/MRR@10 per channel and end-to-end, CI regression gates (1.0 nDCG@10 point), code-retrieval sets (CoIR/CodeSearchNet subsets) for repositories, plus a token-level chunking evaluation (IoU) when chunking changes.

14. Deployment profiles: 'cpu-only on-prem' (BM25 + SPLADE or small dense model + MiniLM cross-encoder; PLAID on CPU if multi-vector), 'gpu' (adds ColBERTv2, monoT5-3B/bge-reranker-large, RankZephyr), 'api' (hosted embeddings + Cohere/LLM rerankers); the same plan schema runs on all, only the registry differs. Secure engineering data by preferring on-prem rerankers (RankZephyr) when confidentiality is required.

15. Expose the component to the wider pipeline via a single call retrieve(task_prompt | explicit_queries, collections, budget{latency_ms, max_cost}, filters, output{k, format}) returning candidates with provenance and the executed plan, so the Pipeline RAG, Task Decomposition, Verification, Parallelization and Caching models can compose it without knowing internals.
pitfalls: Dense-only retrieval out of domain underperforms BM25: on BEIR, DPR averaged -47.7% nDCG@10 vs BM25 and beat it on only 1 of 18 datasets; ANCE -7.4%, TAS-B -2.8% (Thakur et al. 2021). Mitigation: always keep a lexical channel in the fusion and evaluate on an in-domain golden set before deployment.

Under-tuned BM25 baselines hide or fake hybrid gains: the original DPR paper under-reported BM25 (NQ top-20 59.1 vs 62.9 when tuned) and found hybrid did not help on NQ, while the replication with grid-searched fusion weights found +3.2 points (Ma et al. 2021). Mitigation: tune k1/b and the fusion weight on a dev set; log the BM25 baseline alongside every hybrid result.

Tuned RRF constants do not transfer: constants tuned on MS MARCO improved it (0.425 -> 0.451) but degraded HotpotQA (0.675 -> 0.621) (Bruch et al. 2023). Mitigation: keep k = 60 unless re-tuned per collection; prefer convex combination with theoretical min-max normalization when labelled queries exist.

Position bias in the generator: with 20 retrieved documents GPT-3.5-Turbo accuracy fell from 75.8% (gold first) to 53.8% (gold in the middle), below its 56.1% closed-book score; beyond 20 documents only ~1.5% is gained (Liu et al., Lost in the Middle). Mitigation: rerank, place the best passages first, cap passages at 5-20, and consider quote extraction before answering.

Single-vector embeddings saturate on long documents: required dimension grows with document length and normalized margins shrink to ~1e-5 for long BM25-style matching (Luan et al. 2021). Mitigation: short chunks (200-400 tokens), parent/child indexing, or multi-vector / learned-sparse channels for long technical passages.

Hallucinated generative expansion pollutes the index: unfiltered doc2query adds queries not grounded in the passage; filtering with a relevance model gave up to +16% effectiveness, -23% query time, -33% index size (Gospodinov et al., Doc2Query--). Mitigation: cross-encoder filter every synthetic query/summary before indexing; monitor filtered-out samples.

LLM query expansion is slow and expensive and helps strong dense retrievers little: Query2doc costs >2,000 ms per query vs 16 ms BM25 and ~$55k for 550k calls, with gains shrinking to +0.4-0.8 MRR on distilled dense models (Wang et al. 2023). Mitigation: gate behind a router, cache by normalized query, apply mainly to the lexical channel, repeat the original query 5x to prevent drift.

LLM listwise reranking at full depth is impractical online: ~11-32 s and $0.04-$0.60 per query for 100 passages, total $556 for the GPT-4 experiments (Sun et al., RankGPT). Mitigation: cheap reranker first, LLM only over top-20-30 (one-fifth the cost), distil into a 435M cross-encoder (BEIR 53.03 > monoT5-3B 51.36), or use RankZephyr on-prem.

Chunking defaults are often wrong: the common 800-token/400-overlap setting had the worst token-level IoU (1.5) in Chroma's benchmark; semantic chunking gave inconsistent gains and lost to fixed-size on natural documents (HotpotQA 90.6 vs 87.4) (Qu et al. 2024; Chroma 2024). Mitigation: default 200-400 tokens, zero overlap, recursive boundary-aware splitting; evaluate chunking with token-level metrics before adopting semantic chunkers.

Missing or wrong embedding prefixes/instructions: E5 and BGE are trained with asymmetric 'query:'/'passage:' prefixes or query instructions; omitting them degrades retrieval (Wang et al. 2022; Xiao et al. 2023). Mitigation: encode prefix schemes in the model registry and apply automatically.

Post-filtering vector search collapses recall for selective metadata predicates and naive pre-filtering disconnects HNSW graphs (Patel et al., ACORN). Mitigation: predicate-aware traversal (ACORN) or vendor pre-filtering with brute-force fallback for small filtered sets.

Reranker truncation and non-comparable scores: cross-encoders see only the first 512 tokens (BERT-class) or 4,093 tokens (Cohere v3) and their scores are query-dependent, so a fixed global threshold misfires (Cohere best practices). Mitigation: put the contextual header/title first, chunk long records, and calibrate thresholds with 30-50 borderline pairs per domain.

Leaderboard overfitting: MTEB's own conclusion is that no embedding model dominates across tasks (Muennighoff et al.), and most retrievers/rerankers are trained on MS MARCO web queries (Bajaj et al.), so leaderboard rank does not predict performance on specifications, logs or code (CoIR finds code retrieval hard even for SOTA models). Mitigation: in-domain golden sets, code-specific evaluation, and fine-tuning with mined hard negatives.

Index footprint surprises with multi-vector models: uncompressed ColBERT needs 154-286 GiB for 8.8M passages; even ColBERTv2 needs 16-25 GiB (Khattab & Zaharia 2020; Santhanam et al. 2022). Mitigation: budget ~36 bytes per token embedding, use 2-bit residuals and PLAID, and restrict multi-vector indexing to collections that need it.
evaluation_metrics: nDCG@10 (primary ranking-quality metric; graded relevance; BEIR/MTEB/TREC DL standard; Järvelin & Kekäläinen 2002)
Recall@k for k in {20, 100, 1000} (first-stage and fused-pool headroom before reranking; Contriever/HyDE show recall and nDCG can diverge)
MRR@10 (single-correct-passage tasks; MS MARCO dev standard)
Top-k retrieval accuracy / Success@k (answer-bearing passage in top-k; DPR/LoTTE convention) and retrieval failure rate at top-20 (Anthropic contextual retrieval metric)
Token-level recall, precision and IoU of retrieved chunks against labelled evidence spans (Chroma chunking evaluation) for chunking decisions
Channel agreement / overlap@k between lexical and dense lists (drift and complementarity diagnostic) and per-channel contribution to the final top-k
Reranker calibration: score distribution on borderline pairs, precision at the chosen relevance threshold, and 'no relevant result' detection rate
Downstream task metrics with retrieval held fixed vs varied: answer EM/F1 or rubric score at fixed token budget (Dense X, Lost in the Middle protocol), faithfulness/citation accuracy
Latency p50/p95 per stage (first-stage, fusion, rerank tiers) and end-to-end; throughput (queries/s) per deployment profile
Cost per 1,000 queries per stage (embedding, LLM expansion, LLM reranking) and one-time indexing cost per million document tokens
Index size (GB) and build time per channel; re-embedding time on model change
Statistical significance (paired t-test or bootstrap) of nDCG@10 differences on >= 100 queries, with regression gates in CI (e.g. 1.0 nDCG@10 point tolerance)
engineering_adaptation_notes: Source code and repositories: treat code as text for the dense channel (GTE beat prior code retrievers of similar size without code fine-tuning) but add an identifier-aware lexical analyzer (camelCase/snake_case splitting, keep full symbol names) so BM25/SPLADE match function names, error strings and config keys exactly; chunk by syntactic unit (function/class) with file path and module docstring as the contextual header; evaluate on CoIR and CodeSearchNet-style query sets; mine (docstring, function) pairs for in-domain fine-tuning.

Specifications, standards and requirements documents: chunk by clause/requirement ID and keep the numbering, section path and document revision in both the contextual header and metadata; weight the lexical channel higher (alpha ~0.5-0.6) because clause identifiers, units and defined terms must match exactly; use ColBERTv2/PLAID or SPLADE++ for long dense clauses where single vectors saturate (Luan et al.); support traceability queries by indexing cross-references as metadata and allowing filter 'cites: REQ-123'.

Incident reports and postmortems: fields (severity, service, start/end time, root cause category) become filters and ordered key:value text for the reranker; time-range filters must be pushed into the index (ACORN/pre-filter); enable HyDE for exploratory 'has anything like this happened before' queries, but cache results; use LLM listwise reranking offline to build labelled similar-incident sets that train a cheaper cross-encoder.

Test logs and CI output: high-volume, repetitive, identifier-dense text favours BM25/SPLADE with aggressive deduplication (hash identical stack frames) and parent/child indexing (child = individual error block, parent = run summary); use contextual headers with build id, commit, test name; dense retrieval helps mainly for natural-language failure descriptions, so keep alpha low (~0.3-0.4) and calibrate per collection.

CAD/BOM metadata and part catalogues: records are structured, so serialize to YAML-like 'part_number: ..., description: ..., material: ..., supplier: ...' with discriminative fields first (Cohere guidance), index part numbers with an exact-match analyzer, use metadata filters for assembly/revision, and expect BM25/SPLADE to dominate; dense embeddings add value for free-text descriptions and cross-lingual supplier names.

Multi-source engineering queries (e.g. 'which requirements are affected by incident INC-4821 in release 4.2') require the planner to emit several sub-queries against different collections with different channel weights and filters, then a cross-collection fusion keyed by parent document; the Task Decomposition model supplies the sub-queries and the Pipeline RAG model consumes the merged, position-ordered context.

Confidentiality and on-prem constraints: prefer open models for every stage (BM25, SPLADE++, E5/BGE/GTE embedders, ColBERTv2/PLAID, bge-reranker or monoT5, RankZephyr 7B) so no engineering data leaves the network; the 'cpu-only' profile (BM25 + SPLADE + MiniLM cross-encoder, PLAID on CPU) is viable per BEIR and PLAID latency numbers.

Document-level context loss is acute in engineering corpora (a table row or a clause means nothing without its heading), so contextual chunk headers (Anthropic) and title prefixes (DPR) are not optional; measure the top-20 failure rate before and after enrichment on the in-domain golden set.

Golden sets should be built from real engineer queries plus task-decomposer sub-questions, with graded judgments from domain experts; LLM judges can pre-label but specialized content (units, tolerances, standard clause semantics) needs human verification; include 'no relevant document exists' queries to test threshold calibration and abstention.
composition_notes: Task Decomposition -> Hybrid Retrieval: the decomposer turns a complex task prompt into sub-questions, each with inferred filters and collection targets; the retriever's planner consumes these as explicit queries (skipping its own query analysis), runs them in parallel, and returns per-sub-question candidate sets plus a cross-sub-question fused set keyed by parent document. Multi-query decomposition also substitutes for LLM query expansion in many cases, so the router should disable HyDE/Query2doc when the decomposer already produced diverse sub-queries.

Parallelization -> Hybrid Retrieval: channel execution (BM25, SPLADE, dense, ColBERT), per-sub-query retrieval, reranker batching (score 100 pairs in one forward pass; sliding windows of 20 for listwise), and HyDE's N generations are all embarrassingly parallel; the parallelization model should schedule them with the planner's latency budget, and fusion/reranking act as the join points. Index-time enrichment (contextual headers, doc2query, embedding) is a batch map job.

Caching -> Hybrid Retrieval: cache at four levels: (1) embedding cache keyed by (model version, text hash) to avoid re-encoding repeated queries/chunks; (2) LLM expansion cache (HyDE/Query2doc outputs) keyed by normalized query; (3) fused-candidate cache keyed by (plan hash, filters, index version) with short TTL; (4) reranker score cache keyed by (reranker version, query hash, chunk id). Prompt caching of the full parent document makes contextual chunk headers affordable (~$1.02 per million tokens). Any model-registry or index-version change must invalidate the corresponding cache tier.

Answer Verification -> Hybrid Retrieval: the retriever returns calibrated relevance scores, provenance and exact spans so the verifier can check that each claim is grounded in a retrieved passage (quote extraction, as recommended in Anthropic's long-context guidance); low max-rerank-score results should trigger the verifier to flag 'insufficient evidence' instead of answering; the verifier can also issue follow-up retrieval calls (retrieve-verify-retrieve loop) and its failures become hard negatives/new golden-set queries for calibration.

Pipeline RAG -> Hybrid Retrieval: the RAG orchestrator owns the generator prompt and consumes the retriever's position-ordered, XML-packaged context (best passages first, 5-20 passages, documents before the question); it should pass the generator's token budget to the planner so k and chunk expansion are sized accordingly, and implement the corpus-size router (under ~200k tokens: whole-corpus prompt with caching instead of retrieval).

Prompting best practices: the planner and the listwise reranker are prompt-driven LLM calls, so they should use structured outputs (JSON plan, permutation strings), few-shot examples drawn from the collection, temperature 0, and versioned prompts in the model registry; retrieved documents go at the top of the generator prompt with the query at the end (up to 30% quality gain reported by Anthropic), wrapped in tagged <document> blocks with source metadata for citation.

Evaluation across components: retrieval metrics (nDCG@10, Recall@100) must be reported alongside end-task metrics with retrieval held fixed, because reader accuracy saturates before retriever recall (Lost in the Middle); the verification model's grounding checks double as weak relevance labels, and the caching model's hit rates feed the cost model that the planner uses to choose reranker tiers.

Architecture principle shared with all components: every stage is a pure function over a typed Candidate list with provenance, declared cost/latency, and a version; this lets the orchestrator reorder, parallelize, cache and A/B stages without code changes, which is the same contract the other five models should implement.
